newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Congress approves debt rescue fund.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Congress approves debt rescue fund.

text.p: Venezuela's Congress approved plans to set up a Debt Rescue Fund that would be used to pay down domestic and foreign debt, including Bradies, with windfall oil revenues, legislators said.
The bill now goes for a final signing by the executive before it is passed into law.
The fund will be managed by a panel made up of representatives from the ministries of Finance, Energy and Mines, the National Investment Fund and two other members named by the President.
Gonzalez said the fund could be used to pay interest as well as principal, but could not be used to meet payments due in 1997.
"The fund can't be used to offset budgeted debt payments due in 1997, but for can be used from 1998 onwards." However debt, once bought, cannot be resold, "it has to be extinguished," Gonzalez added.

Venezuelan Brady debt prices have firmed in recent months on the possibility of buy-backs, analysts say. Venezuela has some $18 billion worth of Brady debt outstanding, and around another $6 billion of non-restructured debt.
